content: Goal: design one in-scope mechanism coupling TRAINING-ONLY behaviour with hyperbolic geometry inside the baseline RQ-VAE level-1 Sinkhorn assignment, without replacing balanced assignment by argmin. Read: workspace contains only progress.jsonl; external contract file tools/research/contracts/HYPERBOLIC_GEOMETRY_CONTRACT.md was not readable from this session, so I use the contract formulas restated in the task: Poincare ball negative curvature c, radius R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||). Observation: the round explicitly requires a level-1 balanced Sinkhorn whose cost matrix carries BOTH curved distance and a behaviour offset, plus a differentiable curvature-homophily term on the same level-1 soft assignment. Reasoning: use training-graph local triangle cohesion as a bounded rank-normalised behaviour-curvature signal rho_i; put rho_i times the codebook's hyperbolic radial coordinate inside the level-1 cost; keep the baseline Sinkhorn balanced assignment exactly; add a graph-edge curvature-homophily contrastive term on the same soft assignment P, gated by hyperbolic item distance. Geometry-off is c=0 Euclidean branch; behaviour-off zeroes rho and the term. No ablation arm is trained this round. Still open: none; final JSON answer drafted next.

  "idea_id": "hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1",
  "title": "Curvature-Homophilous Hyperbolic Sinkhorn for Behaviour-Consistent Semantic ID Prefixes",
  "motivation": "RQ-VAE Semantic IDs cluster items by latent reconstruction geometry, so the level-1 prefix can mix items whose training-time transition/co-consumption behaviour is structurally very different. A generative recommender then has to predict a coarse code whose meaning is not behaviour-coherent. The mechanism makes level-1 prefix groups homogeneous in a training-only behaviour-graph curvature proxy while preserving the baseline Sinkhorn codebook balancing and the frozen Stage-3 protocol.",
  "novelty": "Unlike Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment, behaviour-suffix rerankers, and standalone hyperbolic regularisers, this mechanism places the behaviour term and the curved term in the SAME level-1 Sinkhorn cost and in the SAME soft-assignment regulariser. The behaviour signal is a graph-local triangle-cohesion curvature proxy, and the codebook has an explicit hyperbolic radial coordinate. The baseline balanced assignment is retained; no argmin replaces Sinkhorn.",
  "key_change": "Level-1 cost becomes C_ik = d_c(z_i,q_k)/D_med - lambda*rho_i*rhat_k, where rho_i is training-graph local cohesion rank and rhat_k is the centred hyperbolic radius of code k; the same balanced Sinkhorn P is regularised by a graph-edge curvature-homophily contrastive loss. Reconstruction and residual recursion still use the unboosted Euclidean codewords e_k.",
  "specification": "1) Build a training-only undirected co-occurrence graph from consecutive transitions in the training split: count_ab increments for each consecutive (a,b), symmetrise, edge weight A_ab=log1p(count_ab). Keep at most d_max=32 highest-weight neighbours per item (fixed memory default, item-id tie-break). For each item i, triangle count t_ij=|N(i) intersect N(j)| and cohesion coh_i = mean_{j in N(i)} log1p(t_ij); isolated items get coh_i=0. Rank-normalise over all training items: rho_i = 2*rank(coh_i)/(N-1)-1 in [-1,1]. Freeze graph, A and rho before Stage 2; no validation or test interaction enters.\n2) Fix Poincare curvature c=1/R^2, R=median_i ||u_i||_2 over the first training minibatch at step 0 (if R<1e-8 set c=1). Fix D_med=median positive d_c(z_i,q_k) over the same batch (if <1e-8 use 1). Map u_i -> z_i=exp_0^c(u_i), e_k -> q_k=exp_0^c(e_k); reconstruction uses e_k only.\n3) Level-1 cost: C_ik = d_c(z_i,q_k)/D_med - lambda*rho_i*rhat_k, with lambda=1 documented dimensionless default, rhat_k = h_k - mean_l h_l, h_k = tanh(d_c(0,q_k)/R_c) for c>0 (and h_k=||e_k||/(1+||e_k||) for the c=0 control).\n4) Run the baseline balanced Sinkhorn on C with unchanged temperature tau and iteration count T: log-domain row/column scalings with uniform marginals r_i=1/B, c_k=1/K1. Hard level-1 index is argmax_k P_ik from this balanced P (baseline rule), not argmin of C.\n5) Add L_curv = (1/|E_B|) sum_{(i,j) in E_B} (A_ij/Abar) * g_ij * [ (1-delta_ij)*(1-s_ij) + delta_ij*s_ij ], where E_B are graph edges induced by the minibatch, Abar is the global mean edge weight, delta_ij=|rho_i-rho_j|/2 in [0,1], s_ij is cosine similarity of P_i and P_j, and g_ij=exp(-d_c(z_i,z_j)/R_c) for c>0 (Euclidean analogue with R_0 for c=0). Total loss = baseline reconstruction + baseline commitment + L_curv. Levels 2 and 3, dimensions, 3-level codebook, optimiser, epochs, batch size and seed are unchanged.",
  "cost_estimate": "Frozen scale: 24,556 training items, 2

4 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 Stage-2 steps. Extra per step over baseline: O(B*K1) for the level-1 behaviour/radius offset; the Sinkhorn itself keeps the baseline T*O(B*K1); L_curv costs O(|E_B|*K1) for the cosine similarities and their backward. With B~1024, d_max=32, |E_B|<=16,384 and K1=256 this is about 4.2M similarity multiply-adds plus roughly 2x backward per step, small relative to the encoder and well under a 5-10 percent wall-clock increase. One-time graph construction is O(sum_i deg_i * min(deg_i,d_max)) over 24,556 items and stores O(E) edges. No extra epochs, cards, early stopping, seeds or sweep runs.",
  "falsifiable_hypothesis": "If the coupling is real, the level-1 hard assignments and the encoder/codebook gradients will change relative to the behaviour-off and c=0 Euclidean controls, L1-sharing pairs will be more behaviour-curvature homogeneous than random pairs, Sinkhorn level-1 usage will remain near-uniform, and the single Stage-3 run will yield test Recall@10 above 0.065. If the single run does not exceed 0.065, or homogeneity is no better than random while usage stays balanced, the mechanism is not worth keeping.",
  "risks": [
    "Triangle cohesion may still encode popularity or hub structure despite rank normalisation, so rho_i may not be a clean behaviour-curvature signal.",
    "The centred codebook radius rhat_k may take an arbitrary sign, so the behaviour offset can fight reconstruction before the contrastive term corrects it.",
    "The graph-edge homophily term can over-smooth assignments and reduce effective codebook use; Sinkhorn balances columns but hard argmax may still concentrate.",
    "Stage-3 Recall may be limited by decoder capacity or SID length rather than by prefix semantics.",
    "The Poincare exp map can saturate for large latent norms and produce small gradients.",
    "Top-32 graph truncation may discard long-tail structure relevant to niche items.",
    "A single run and single seed make the result sensitive to seed noise."
  ],
  "behavior_signal": "Training-only local triangle cohesion of an undirected item co-occurrence graph, rank-normalised into a bounded behaviour-curvature proxy rho_i in [-1,1].",
  "behavior_computation": "From the training split only: for every training sequence, increment an undirected count for each consecutive item pair, symmetrise, and set A_ab=log1p(count_ab). For each of the 24,556 training items, keep the top d_max=32 neighbours by A_ab (item-id tie-break); compute t_ij=|N(i) intersect N(j)|; set coh_i=mean_{j in N(i)} log1p(t_ij), or 0 if the item has no neighbours; rank-normalise coh over all training items with average ranks to get rho_i. The graph is frozen before Stage 2 and is never rebuilt from validation or test.",
  "leakage_boundary": "The graph, A_ij, rho_i, curvature c, D_med and all SID codebook training use only the training split and the first training minibatch. No validation or test interaction, transition, co-consumption event or label enters graph construction, cost construction, curvature estimation, or codebook initialisation. Stage-3 test Recall@10 is used only after training as evaluation.",
  "hyperbolic_operator": "Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c=1/R^2, with R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x) plus y||), and exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||). The curved terms are d_c in the level-1 Sinkhorn cost, d_c in the graph-edge gate g_ij, and the codebook radial coordinate h_k=tanh(d_c(0,

q_k)/R_c).",
  "hyperbolic_location": "Level-1 quantisation only: the level-1 Sinkhorn cost matrix, the level-1 soft assignment used by L_curv, and the level-1 codebook radial coordinate. Levels 2 and 3 and all reconstruction/residual recursion remain Euclidean and use unboosted codewords.",
  "coupling_path": "Training graph -> rho_i -> level-1 cost offset C_ik and pair curvature difference delta_ij; encoder latent -> z_i -> d_c -> the SAME C_ik and the edge gate g_ij; balanced Sinkhorn(C) -> P -> L_curv and -> hard k1=argmax(P). Removing behaviour zeroes rho, A and L_curv, changing C and the loss; removing geometry sets c=0, changing d_c, h_k and g_ij. Thus neither side is an unused suffix and both change the core computation.",
  "coupling_equation": "C_ik = d_c(z_i,q_k)/D_med - lambda*rho_i*rhat_k, and L_curv = (1/|E_B|)*sum_{(i,j) in E_B} (A_ij/Abar)*exp(-d_c(z_i,z_j)/R_c)*[(1-delta_ij)*(1-s_ij)+delta_ij*s_ij], with delta_ij=|rho_i-rho_j|/2 and s_ij=cos(P_i,P_j).",
  "observables": "Report L1 hard code usage/ER, L2 prefix count, L3 collision rate, L3 refinement gain, and Stage-3 test Recall@10. Also report behaviour-curvature prefix homogeneity H = mean_{pairs sharing L1} (1-|rho_i-rho_j|/2) minus the same mean over random item pairs, together with Sinkhorn column-usage entropy. The expected observable is higher H than random pairing, near-baseline level-1 usage balance, and test Recall@10 above 0.065.",
  "ablation_behavior_off": "Code switch behaviour_active=False: set rho_i=0, A_ij=0 and L_curv=0; keep the full hyperbolic cost d_c, rhat_k, balanced Sinkhorn and all other training unchanged. This arm exists in code and is not trained this round.",
  "ablation_geometry_off": "Code switch c=0: use Euclidean d_0(x,y)=||x-y||, z_i=u_i, q_k=e_k, h_k=||e_k||/(1+||e_k||), and g_ij=exp(-||z_i-z_j||/R_0) with R_0 measured from the first training minibatch; behaviour offset and L_curv remain on. This is the same-capacity Euclidean control and must be run as an independent control arm in a separate round, never as a trained ablation here.",
  "ablation_both_on": "Full coupled run: c>0 from the measured training latent scale, behaviour_active=True with rho from the frozen training graph, curved cost, curved edge gate and L_curv all on, balanced Sinkhorn retained.",
  "spec_equations": "DIMENSIONS: u_i,z_i in R^D; level-1 e_k,q_k in R^D, k=1..K1=256; C,P in R^{B x K1}; rho in R^B; A sparse B x B; delta,s,g in R^{|E_B|}. GRADIENT_RULES: rho, A, c, D_med, R_c and Abar are detached constants; P is differentiable through the log-domain Sinkhorn; L_curv backpropagates through cos(P_i,P_j) and through g_ij's d_c(z_i,z_j) to the encoder; the hard index k1=argmax_k P_ik is used only through the baseline straight-through estimator for reconstruction, with no gradient through argmax; e_k is updated by the baseline commitment/codebook objective. TRAINING_INTEGRATION: replace only the level-1 cost and add L_curv to the baseline loss; keep the baseline 3 levels, dimensions, codebook sizes, optimiser, 3000 epochs, 24 steps/epoch, batch size and seed; no early stopping. CONVENTIONS: c>0 fixed negative curvature; Poincare ball radius R_c=1/sqrt(c); reconstruction and residual recursion use unboosted e_k; level-1 assignment is the baseline balanced Sinkhorn, never argmin(C). Equations: d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x) plus y||); z_i=exp_0^c(u_i); q_k=exp_0^c(e_k); h_k=tanh(d_c(0,q_k)/R_c); rhat_k=h_k-(1/K1)*sum_l h_l; C_ik=d_c(z_i,q_k)/D_med-lambda*

rho_i*rhat_k; P=BalancedSinkhorn(C,tau,T) with log-domain updates log_alpha_i=-logsumexp_k(-C_ik/tau+log_beta_k)+log(1/B), log_beta_k=-logsumexp_i(-C_ik/tau+log_alpha_i)+log(1/K1), P_ik=exp(-C_ik/tau+log_alpha_i+log_beta_k); delta_ij=|rho_i-rho_j|/2; s_ij=cos(P_i,P_j); g_ij=exp(-d_c(z_i,z_j)/R_c); L_curv=(1/|E_B|)*sum_{(i,j) in E_B}(A_ij/Abar)*g_ij*((1-delta_ij)*(1-s_ij)+delta_ij*s_ij); L=L_baseline_recon+L_baseline_commit+mu*L_curv with mu=1 documented dimensionless default; k1_i=argmax_k P_ik with STE. c=0 branch replaces d_c by d_0, z by u, q by e, and h_k by ||e_k||/(1+||e_k||).",
  "spec_inputs_outputs": "Inputs: minibatch unboosted latents u (B x D), level-1 Euclidean codebook e (K1 x D), frozen training-graph edge weights A and behaviour ranks rho, fixed c, D_med, tau, T, lambda=1, mu=1. Outputs: level-1 cost C (B x K1), balanced soft assignment P (B x K1), hard level-1 indices k1 (B), centred code radius rhat (K1), and scalar L_curv. The operator is called once per training step before reconstruction and level-2/3 residual coding.",
  "safeguards": "Compute Poincare maps and distances in fp32; clamp the Moebius-add norm argument to 1-1e-12 before artanh; keep z_i and q_k strictly inside the ball because exp_0^c uses tanh; if R<1e-8 set c=1; if D_med<1e-8 set D_med=1; if R_0<1e-8 set R_0=1. Run Sinkhorn in log domain with logsumexp and the baseline T; renormalise P to the uniform marginals and assert finite values. Clamp cosines to [-1,1], delta to [0,1], rho to [-1,1], and skip L_curv for a batch with |E_B|=0. Detach all graph and scale constants. Keep lambda=1 and mu=1 as fixed documented dimensionless defaults, never tuned. Monitor level-1 column usage/entropy and hard code counts; do not replace the balanced assignment with argmin. Apply the baseline gradient clipping and mixed-precision policy, with distance computations in fp32."
}
